''"Combat automaton which became self-aware. Ancient technology allows manipulation of Orbs."'' {{Icon|}}
The '''Defect''' is one of four playable characters in Slay the Spire. Once among the like of [[Orb Walker]]s and [[Bronze Automaton]] as one of many ancient automatons, it has since gained sentience and seeks its way out of the Spire. It attacks foes with a high-tech arsenal, array of [[Power]]s, and elemental evocations. The Defect has a unique mechanic, the [[Orbs]]. Using cards and Relics, The Defect Channels these elemental spheres into a set of Orb slots, activating their passive effects each turn or Evoking them for a one-time burst. The Defect starts with three Orb slots, though cards and relics can add or {{C|Consume|consume}} them. It starts with 75 hp. The Defect's starting [[Relic]] is {{R|Cracked Core}}, which Channels 1 Lightning at the start of each combat. It was added to the beta build in [https://steamcommunity.com/games/646570/announcements/detail/1667898210977004105 Weekly Patch 22: Testing the Third Character] during the early access. It was [https://steamcommunity.com/games/646570/announcements/detail/1714084208003916507 released] to the public, along with the game and [[Ironclad|other]] [[Silent|two]] characters on January 23rd, 2019. ==Cards== ===Starting Deck=== * 4 {{C|Strike_B}} * 4 {{C|Defend_B}} * 1 {{C|Zap}} * 1 {{C|Dualcast}} {{Defect Card Navbox}} ==Gameplay== ===Orbs=== ''Main article: [[Orbs]]'' The Defect begins with three [[Orb]] slots and considers the rightmost Orb to be the 'next' Orb to Evoke. Channelling an Orb inserts it into the rightmost empty slot. If every slot is full, each Orb will be shifted one slot to the right, popping the right-most Orb out of its slot and Evoking it. The Defect can have a maximum of 10 Orb slots. {{KW|Lightning}}, {{KW|Frost}} and {{KW|Dark}} orbs have a passive effect that activates at the end of the Defect's turn, from right to left, or oldest to newest. The passive effect of {{KW|Plasma}} activates at the start of the Defect's turn. While these effects are initially weak, The Defect can increase {{KW|Focus}} and channel additional copies to sharply increase their potency. === Focus === ''Main article: {{KW|Focus}}'' '''{{KW|Focus}}''' is a stat unique to [[The Defect]] that affects Orbs the same way {{KW|Strength}} affects Attacks and {{KW|Dexterity}} affects {{KW|Block}}. Increasing {{KW|Focus}} increases the magnitude of both the passive and {{KW|Evoke}} effects of each Orb (except for {{KW|Plasma}}). It is possible to reduce Orb effects to 0 by decreasing {{KW|Focus}}. == Relics== The Defect has fewer class-specific relics than the other classes, having only one class-specific rare relic rather than three (like the [[Ironclad]] and [[Silent]]) or two (like the [[Watcher]]). The Watcher has equally few overall, but instead of being short two Rare relics is short one Rare and one Boss relic. Starting Relic: {{R|Cracked Core}} Common Relic: {{R|Data Disk}} Uncommon Relics: {{R|Gold-Plated Cables}}, {{R|Symbiotic Virus}} Rare Relics: {{R|Emotion Chip}} Boss Relics: {{R|Frozen Core}} (replaces {{R|Cracked Core}}), {{R|Inserter}}, {{R|Nuclear Battery}} Shop Relic: {{R|Runic Capacitor}} == Strategy == The Defect's game plan almost always involves implementing a long-term plan each battle. By developing [[Orbs]], Powers, and cards with escalating effects, the Defect sets up an insurmountable late-game position and then destroys its enemies with its accumulated advantage. This is a radically different style from [[Silent|the Silent]] and [[Ironclad|the Ironclad]], who tend to apply bursts of damage to take enemies out opportunistically. Due to the nature of this approach to deckbuilding, the Defect may struggle in the early-game, when it is not capable of producing such unbreakable barriers on command. However, the Defect inarguably has one of the highest peaks regarding sheer dominance out of all characters - one example is the "Frost Turtle" build, which, when heavily optimized, allows the Defect to gain hundreds of block per turn consistently. Even the tankiest and most heavy-hitting enemies may be completely outclassed by the Defect. However, the Defect notably struggles to win with a deck full of "good stuff". While it does have access to some individually strong cards, they don't present the sheer power that the other characters enjoy without support. However, due to the long-term nature of its best strategies, the Defect must sometimes take such individually strong cards, either to survive the first few acts or to provide frontloaded solutions while it sets up. Juggling deckbuilding decisions between these two extremes of short-term benefit v.s. long-term power is thus an ongoing struggle during every Defect run, yet a rewarding one once all of the pieces fall into place. The Defect also has a higher number of chance-based effects, like {{C|Hello World}}, {{C|Chaos}}, and {{C|Creative AI}}. The Defect's strongly synergistic cards encourage some powerful and well-supported archetypes. Identifying and focusing on one is a key aspect of the Defect strategy. === Build types === Listed below are the standard synergies that Defect decks build towards, which may give you an idea of direction for your own runs. Some important things to keep in mind: *Most of these builds aren't mutually exclusive. Think of each of the archetypes listed below as an engine that you can incorporate into your deck; depending on the situation, you are more than able to adapt or combine multiple of them. *It's important to not "force" a particular build from the outset of the game. Build your deck to solve your immediate problems first and foremost, then allow an archetype to come to you organically. The only exception would be if you run into cards or relics in the early-game that are both individually impactful ''and'' form the crux of an entire archetype, and such situations are few and far between. {{Archetype|{{KW|Focus}} Stacking |text=While Defect's orbs are initially weak, they grow in power significantly once it finds {{KW|Focus}}-increasing cards for its Deck. After this, the Defect's game plan shifts to playing all of them as quickly as possible, then becoming incredibly powerful in terms of offense and defense. Generally, the Defect wants a mix of different kinds of orbs; in particular, you should be able to consistently generate {{KW|Lightning}} and {{KW|Frost}}, changing between them to suit the situation at hand. Cards or relics that increase {{KW|Focus}}: *{{R|Data Disk}} gives +1 Focus for free, helping you significantly at the start of a battle. *{{C|Defragment}} is your bread-and-butter, and are priority upgrades. *{{C|Biased Cognition}} provides a large burst of Focus which can help you end hallway fights quickly. Its downside can be negated with {{R|Orange Pellets}} or blocked by your own {{KW|Artifact}}. Combo this with {{C|Core Surge}} or {{R|Clockwork Souvenir}} to gain permanent Focus with no drawback. *{{R|Inserter}} is an absolute must because it provides more orb slots to make good usage of the focus. {{C|Capacitor}} is also a must in this regard. **{{C|Consume}} is a more situational Focus gain card as it reduces your orb slots, but it is reusable as it is a Skill and not a Power. **{{R|The Boot}} combined with {{C|Barrage}} adds a surprisingly amount of damage especially with the max out orb slots. Cards that generate {{KW|Lightning}} and {{KW|Frost}}: *{{C|Zap}} (Zap+ is 0 cost) *{{C|Ball Lightning}} *{{C|Electrodynamics}} is a very high-impact card against multiple enemies and is generally the Defect's main AoE solve. *{{C|Cold Snap}} *{{C|Glacier}} *{{C|Coolheaded}} provides card draw while channeling Frost, allowing you to dig for your main cards. Other helpful additions: *{{C|Capacitor}} and relics such as {{R|Inserter}} and {{R|Runic Capacitor}} give you more Orb slots to benefit from Focus increasing Orb value. *{{C|Seek}} lets you pull your Focus-generating cards immediately out of the Deck. *Card draw such as {{C|Skim}} and {{C|Compile Driver}} can help cycle through your Deck to get Focus into play as soon as possible, especially when combined with {{KW|Energy}} generators. **{{C|Fission}} is the best of both worlds, providing both card draw and Energy! *{{C|Force Field}} can help generate {{KW|Block}} in a pinch. *{{C|Echo Form}} can duplicate your {{C|Defragment|Defragments}} which can normally only be played once, or give you multiple Orb casts. *{{C|Chaos}}+ can give you a large volume of orbs right away, but be wary of leaving orb generation up to chance against elites or bosses... }} {{Archetype|{{KW|Frost}} Turtle |text=While running {{KW|Lightning}}-only is a risky prospect, {{KW|Frost}}-only builds are surprisingly consistent and can thrive even against the true final boss. Once the shields are up, the Defect can devote every Energy to damage while the opposition cannot do anything back to it. Frost Turtle builds require {{KW|Focus}} and orb slot buffs to function. Refer to the Focus Stacking section for more information on these cards and relics. *Cards that generate {{KW|Frost}} include {{C|Cold Snap}}, {{C|Glacier}}, and {{C|Coolheaded}}. *Cards and relics that generate {{KW|Focus}} include {{C|Defragment}}, {{C|Biased Cognition}}, {{C|Consume}}, and {{R|Data Disk}}. *Cards and relics that add orb slots include {{C|Capacitor}}, {{R|Inserter}}, and {{R|Runic Capacitor}}. Your main priority as you approach endgame should be to find a damage solution for the final bosses, as defense alone might not win you the run. *{{C|Barrage}} is one of your best options in this slot-based deck. *{{C|Blizzard}} may seem tempting, but it scales up very slowly, and takes a long time to match Barrage's power. It is still a viable option if you need spread damage. *Combine this build with {{KW|Dark}} Orb-generating cards and let them build up behind your Frost orbs, unleashing them when the time is right. *Using a mix of regular block such as {{C|Boot Sequence}} and {{C|Charge Battery}} can add to the Frost Orbs. Relics that provide block such as {{R|Anchor}} and {{R|Captain's Wheel}} are extremely useful. **Avoid {{C|Force Field}} unless you have enough powers to get it down 2 or less. **{{R|Orichalcum}} on the other hand is useful for an extra passive block because it activates before the Frost orbs and is especially useful in early runs. Other tips and useful additions: *{{R|Calipers}} is a run-winning addition to this deck. The Defect will often have leftover {{KW|Block}} with a full setup, which this relic allows to snowball out of control. **{{C|Reinforced Body}} provides a decent emergency card in case you don't have much orbs or little focus. *For orb slots, 2 copies of {{C|Capacitor}} should suffice, but you can take more if you want. *Take as many {{C|Defragment}} as possible, and upgrade as many of them as you can. Focus is even more crucial for this deck as 1 Focus means 1 additional {{KW|Block}} per channeled Frost orb. **Since {{C|Capacitor}} and {{C|Defragment}} are not expensive, {{R|Mummified Hand}} has an even greater chance to allow multiple free cards to be played. *{{C|Loop}} like {{C|Defragment}} is a must , especially if upgraded or multiple copies. *The {{R|Frozen Core}} boss relic fills your orb slots with Frost orbs, which can help you more quickly establish your defenses. *{{R|Runic Dome}} is also a powerful boss relic for this Deck, as the extra energy helps get everything into play. You will generally not care about the enemy's action once set up. *Multiple copies of {{C|Go for the Eyes}} provides a similar strategy to the [[Silent|Silent's]] {{KW|Weak}}-chaining strategy. }} {{Archetype|{{KW|Lightning}} Spam |text=This aggressive build tries to channel and Evoke as many {{KW|Lightning}} Orbs as possible, beating enemies down eight damage at a time. Unlike other Orb builds, smaller is better - one Orb slot is optimal to facilitate Evoking. Key cards to this build: *Cards that generate {{KW|Lightning}} include {{C|Zap}}, {{C|Ball Lightning}}, and {{C|Electrodynamics}}. **Electrodynamics is a key {{C|Seek}} or {{R|Bottled Tornado}} target, letting you start fights against multiple enemies with a massive advantage. *If you have a large number of powers, {{C|Storm}} can add value to those plays by generating even more Lightning. *{{C|Bullseye}} becomes significantly stronger when you're constantly evoking Lightning in the target's direction, amplifying all that damage. *{{C|Consume}} decreases the number of orb slots while increasing Focus. With fewer orb slots, you can rapidly Evoke multiple Lightning Orbs for a large amount of damage. *{{C|Static Discharge}} turns the enemy's offense against them, channeling massive amounts of Lightning against multi-hits in particular. **As you are willingly inviting damage to end fights, one or two copies of {{C|Self Repair}} are recommended to keep the Defect's health at safe levels. *{{C|Thunder Strike}} and {{C|Tempest}} are this deck's premier finishers, dumping huge volumes of damage onto the enemy. **{{KW|Energy}} generation from cards like {{C|Aggregate}}, {{C|TURBO}}, or {{C|Double Energy}} thus helps this build quite a bit. Other considerations: *Have a {{KW|Block}} plan in mind, as you will gain much less value from {{KW|Frost}} if you are constantly Evoking everything. For example, if you are supporting {{C|Tempest}} with Energy generators, you can use {{C|Reinforced Body}} as well to defend yourself from huge hits. *This build benefits greatly from damage mitigation relics such as {{R|Torii}} or {{R|Tungsten Rod}}, especially in conjunction with {{C|Static Discharge}}. When combined, they can completely nullify damage from almost all multi-hits. }} {{Archetype|{{KW|Dark}} Orb Engine |text=Even though the tricky {{KW|Dark}} Orbs aren't as well-supported as the others and don't always fit into typical builds, the satisfaction of Evoking a highly charged Dark Orb twice (or more!) makes it all worthwhile to try. Cards and relics that generate Dark Orbs: *{{C|Darkness}} is your main {{KW|Dark}} Orb generator. When upgraded, it powers up all Dark Orbs in play by one charge. *{{C|Doom and Gloom}} is a solid spread damage option that happens to generate a Dark Orb. This card is what usually fits into a normal build as an early-game option, but gets to shine a lot more here. *{{R|Symbiotic Virus}} generates a free Dark Orb at the start of each combat. Key parts of a Dark Orb engine: *{{C|Recursion}} is arguably the most important card for Dark Orbs. This is because if you Evoke a Dark Orb with Recursion, it will immediately channel again with the same stats. If you have a Dark Orb in front but don't want to give it up quite yet, Recursion will move it to the back while dealing a huge chunk of damage in the process, letting you continue building its power. *{{C|Dualcast}} and {{C|Multi-Cast}} will unleash the Dark Orb multiple times onto enemies, usually ending the fight with a sufficient charge. **If running Multi-Cast, you will want to support it with {{KW|Energy}} generating cards like {{C|Aggregate}}, {{C|TURBO}}, or {{C|Double Energy}}. Other considerations: *Keep in mind that the Dark orb will target the lowest health enemy. *This engine works well with {{KW|Frost}} decks, as Frost Orbs help generate {{KW|Block}} and allow you to stall the fight until you are ready to Evoke a Dark Orb. *Be extremely careful when fighting enemies with the ability to gain [[Intangible]] (namely [[Nemesis]]), as evoking a Dark orb at the wrong time will result in the target taking only 1 damage and the accumulated charges being wasted as a result. }} {{Archetype|Zero Cost |text=The Defect has a high number of strong 0-cost cards, as well as unique supporting cards like {{C|Scrape}} and {{C|All for One}} and efficient card-draw Skills. Drown an enemy under {{C|FTL|FTLs}}, {{C|Claw|Claws}}, and {{C|Beam Cell|Beam Cells}}. It's sort of like the Silent's {{C|Shiv}} builds, but way more back-loaded and visually impressive. Damage comes from 0-cost cards that do damage: *{{C|Claw}} *{{C|FTL}} *{{C|Beam Cell}} *{{C|Go for the Eyes}} *{{C|Streamline}} - requires 2 plays (of 2- and 1-cost respectively) before it reaches 0 cost. *{{C|Dualcast}}+ *{{C|Zap}}+ The Deck then also needs a lot of recycle/card-draw effects to get as many of the 0-cost cards in play per turn. The Defect has a lot of great support cards for this type of deck: *{{C|All for One}} - the best one for this deck as it allows you to re-play all of your 0-cost cards you've played in your deck up until that point *{{C|Rebound}} - allows you to double-play cards like {{C|Streamline}} and {{C|Claw}} to more quickly ramp up their effects. *{{C|Hologram}} - reuse {{C|All for One}}, double-play {{C|Streamline}}, or replay a 0-cost card. *{{C|Scrape}} - good card draw that let's you immediately play any 0-cost cards it finds. *{{C|White Noise}}+ - when upgraded it becomes a free power. *{{C|Reboot}} - very good if you already have the core engine of your deck in place. *{{C|Seek}} - great for finding {{C|Claw}}, or even better, {{C|All for One}}. There are also some extremely useful neutral cards that either help get 0-cost cards, or are 0-cost cards themselves (or both): *{{C|Madness}} - can be difficult to get, but if you are able to acquire it, it will greatly speed up your deck by turning your strongest cards into 0-cost cards. ** 2 {{C|Madness}}+ with {{C|All for One}} and {{C|Hologram}}+ is an infinite. Use both madness to reduce {{C|All for One}} and {{C|Hologram}}+ to 0-cost, and use each one to put the other back into your hand. **{{C|Seek}}+ makes this easier to pull off. Double Seek+ is even easier, as it allows for 3 of the 4 cards to be put into your hand immediately. **{{R|Bottled Lightning}} also makes this easier to pull off. *{{C|Swift Strike}} *{{C|Secret Technique}}+/{{C|Secret Weapon}}+ - both of these when upgraded will allow you to get your key cards faster. *{{C|Panache}} - as you will almost certainly be playing more than 5 cards every turn, this will be a guaranteed 10 damage to all enemies every turn. *{{C|Thinking Ahead}} - upgrade this ASAP so that you can reuse it. *{{C|Violence}} *{{C|Metamorphosis}} *{{C|Purity}} - can get rid of Strikes/Defends during combat, which, depending on the state of your deck, may allow you to go infinite. *{{C|J.A.X.}} - a rare card as it only comes from the [[Augmenter]] event, but any source of strength is a huge benefit for a deck that aims to play many 0-cost attacks every turn. As an added bonus, the card itself costs 0 and so, if you have the health for it, can quickly ramp up your damage to high levels in this deck. }} {{Archetype|Power Spam |text=The Ironclad likes Attacks, the Silent loves Skills, and the Defect completes the cycle with its affinity for Powers. Grab high-impact powers like {{C|Echo Form}}, pick up some {{C|Force Field|Force Fields}}, stack powerful effects, and bury the opposition under your cumulative advantage. While most Defect builds pick and choose the most appropriate Powers for their deck, this one will eventually have the benefits of them all. There is nothing quite like being able to double your first 6 cards played per turn with 10+ {{KW|Focus}} and a horde of {{KW|Lightning}} orbs staring down any boss that dares stand in your way. Refine the deck by using Powers to fill the roles of Attacks and Skills. Consider {{C|Static Discharge}} and {{C|Storm}} your primary sources of damage, and {{C|Buffer}} and {{C|Self Repair}} your biggest blockers. A Power spam deck's win condition depends on the particular Powers you acquire. Most builds will create a huge amount of {{KW|Lightning}}, but others simply lean on {{C|Creative AI}} and let the buffs snowball out of control. Key cards and relics for this build: *{{C|Storm}} allows the deck to maintain offensive presence while setting up. Upgrade it as soon as you identify that your deck is leaning into Power spam. *{{C|Creative AI}} allows Power spam decks to scale to infinity without ever losing steam, synergizing amazingly with itself and all of the other Power-synergy cards that The Defect can get. *{{C|Heatsinks}} is what makes a Power spam deck tick. It will allow you to blaze through your deck to find key Powers or {{KW|Energy}} generation like {{C|Aggregate}}, {{C|TURBO}}, or {{C|Double Energy}}, which is critical to setting up before you take too much damage. *{{C|Recycle}}+ can delete useless powers that {{C|Creative AI}} generates, such as {{C|Hello World}} or extra copies of Creative AI, and helps keep your deck size thin in longer fights. *{{C|Force Field}} is your main {{KW|Block}} supplement; it is essentially guaranteed to be at 0 cost due to how this deck functions. *{{C|Amplify}}, while a bit inconsistent, can provide a huge power spike depending on which Power is duplicated. Good targets for Amplify are cards like {{C|Defragment}} and {{C|Capacitor}}. If you choose to run it, support it with cards like {{C|Hologram}} and {{C|Equilibrium}} which can get it into your hand at the perfect time. *{{R|Mummified Hand}} is essentially a game-ender in this build. Being able to chain Powers and potentially play your entire hand for free is simply too good to pass up. *The {{R|Bird-Faced Urn}} is the perfect relic to recover HP lost while setting up. }} {{Archetype|{{C|Reprogram}} |text=A deck that repeatedly plays {{C|Reprogram}} to rapidly scale up your {{KW|Strength}} and {{KW|Dexterity}}, ignoring {{KW|Focus}} and Orbs entirely. If you find yourself with a conspicuous lack of Focus deep into the run, Reprogram can give your deck a strong win condition. It is important that you do not force a Reprogram deck, as committing to it too early can completely lock you out of half of Defect's card pool. Key cards and relics: *{{C|Reprogram}} is the star of the show. Upgrade it as soon as possible, and you'll gain +2 {{KW|Strength}} and {{KW|Dexterity}} every time you cycle through your deck. You only really need one copy, and cards like {{C|Seek}} or {{C|Skim}} can help you get to it faster. *A few copies of {{C|Hologram}}+ let you reuse {{C|Reprogram}}, repeatedly play {{C|Steam Barrier}} in an emergency, or recover copies of each other, scaling up your Block as needed. Your high Dexterity will easily make up for Hologram's low Block. *{{C|Echo Form}} allows you to double-play Reprogram at the start of the turn. Double-playing damage or block cards also compensates for the fact that Defect doesn't have many cards (aside from the unreliable {{C|Rip and Tear}}) that scale multiple times with Strength or Dexterity. *{{C|Hyperbeam}} deals massive AoE damage, and you can ignore its only downside. *{{C|Steam Barrier}} also effectively loses its downside, since you'll be gaining Dexterity faster than Steam Barrier loses Block. *{{C|All for One}} strategies fit well with this deck, since spammable 0-costs like {{C|Claw}} and {{C|Beam Cell}} scale well with high Strength. It can also recover your {{C|Steam Barrier}}. *{{KW|Plasma}} generators like {{C|Fusion}}+ and {{R|Nuclear Battery}} are good options, since Plasma Orbs don't scale with Focus. *{{R|Prismatic Shard}}, while usually unreliable, is a surprisingly good relic to pick up when you have Reprogram. Other characters' damage cards scale much better with Strength and Dexterity, letting you better take advantage of the boosts. Reprogram can also shine in a hybrid build. If you find yourself with lots of Orbs but no Focus, the following cards coupled with Reprogram can help speed your Deck up: *{{C|Fission}} allows you to get one last burst of value out of your Orbs by speeding through your Deck, letting you get Reprogram into circulation or finding your Echo Form earlier to begin the snowballing process. *{{C|Barrage}} conditionally scales multiple times with Reprogram's Strength boost. If you have some Plasma generation or still have copies of damage commons such as {{C|Cold Snap}} or {{C|Ball Lightning}} in your Deck that are generating useless Orbs, consider picking this up to still be able to capitalize on their presence. }} {{Archetype|{{R|Snecko Eye}} Abuse |text=The Defect has incredible synergy with the {{R|Snecko Eye}} due to the very large pool of high-impact cards it has. *The Defect has several extremely powerful but expensive cards like {{C|Fusion}}, {{C|Echo Form}}, {{C|Sunder}}, and {{C|Meteor Strike}}. By taking {{R|Snecko Eye}} early enough, you can focus exclusively on taking these cards for absurdly high-value turns. Many of these effects will generate more energy than they spend. **In particular, {{C|Meteor Strike}} will never cost more than 3 Energy, allowing you to always play it. Evoking the {{KW|Plasma}} Orbs it generates can also allow you to play more high-rolled cards, which somewhat negates the drawback of Snecko Eye. *{{C|All for One}} is completely broken with Snecko Eye. Since cards will retain their cost until you draw them again, it will fetch everything that was decremented to 0 cost, even cards that would normally be quite expensive. A 0-cost All for One paired with a 0-cost {{C|Hologram}} (which is also a good card in this build for similar reasons) is an easy infinite. *{{C|Skim}}, {{C|Compile Driver}}, {{C|Coolheaded}}+, and {{C|Overclock}} can provide large amounts of card draw, which is a premium in Snecko decks. *Most of the Defect's 0-cost cards are dead weight in this archetype, so it is important to home in on it as early as possible. If you don't get {{R|Snecko Eye}} from [[Neow]] or the first boss, pick a different strategy. }} {{Archetype|10 Card Infinite |text=With this build, the defect is capable of going infinite against most opponents. * Getting the deck down to 10 cards allows for setting up 4 card infinite cycles with {{C|Skim}} and negative cost cards. *{{C|Fusion}}, {{C|Meteor Strike}}, {{C|TURBO}} (with {{C|Recycle}}), {{C|Recursion}}, {{C|Dualcast}} can combine in various ways to get negative cost. *{{C|Hologram}} or a second {{C|Skim}} can be used to restart the cycle. * Example set: {{C|Skim}}+, {{C|Hologram}}+, {{C|Fusion}}+, {{C|Dualcast}}+. Skim draws Hologram, Fusion and Dual Cast, Fusion and Dual Cast make net 2 energy, Hologram retrieves Skim. Nets 1 energy and 5 block, can substitute any attacks in for Fusion and Dual Cast after energy is built up. * 2 {{C|Coolheaded}}+ and {{C|Fusion}}+ can make infinite block, and channel an arbitrary number of Frost orbs for {{C|Blizzard}}. * It is important to only take cards that are either Powers, Exhaust, or are directly part of the combo while building the deck, since the goal is to get the total number of cards down under 10. Recycle can handle junk put in the deck and help thin it out if its not quite down to 10 cards. * {{C|Boot Sequence}} is very helpful as a free method of preventing damage during the first turn while the infinite combo is being set up while exhausting itself out of the deck to help enable the combo. }} ==Unlocks== The Defect itself is unlocked by completing a run with The Silent. {| class="article-table" !Unlock Number !Prizes Unlocked |- |1st |{{C|Rebound}}, {{C|Equilibrium}}, {{C|Echo Form}} |- |2nd |{{C|TURBO}}, {{C|Sunder}}, {{C|Meteor Strike}} |- |3rd |{{C|Hyperbeam}}, {{C|Recycle}}, {{C|Core Surge}} |- |4th |{{R|Gold-Plated Cables}}, {{R|Turnip}}, {{R|Runic Capacitor}} |- |5th |{{R|Data Disk}}, {{R|Symbiotic Virus}}, {{R|Emotion Chip}} |} ==Gallery== defect1.jpg|The Defect in-game defect2.jpg|The Defect appearing in its Steam Background BiasedCognition.png|The Defect featured prominently in the card art for [[Biased Cognition]] defect4.png|The Defect as it appears in some official artwork for the game defect5.JPG|The Defect's character select screen Gallerypiece.JPG|The Defect seen in the Launch Trailer alongside the [[Ironclad]] and the [[Silent]] [[Category:Class]]
